name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (battle drop-collection helper). No Ghidra address residue. Descriptor accurately reflects body: scans the runtime char array and collects 3-byte drop entries from chars killed by the current attack. The 'dead_char' descriptor is acceptable: although the chars are not yet flagged dead (flags bit0==0) but only lethally wounded (hp_current==0, death animation pending), the function's purpose is exactly to gather the drops left by chars that just died this kill. The sibling fn at 0x1B6B7 (fd2_collect_pending_death_drops) shares the same flag/HP gate and differs only by entry-type filter (type==3 here vs type!=0xFF there); the existing names already distinguish the two by behavior, so renaming is not warranted.
purpose: Scan the runtime char array and copy the 3-byte drop entry of each char freshly killed by the current attack (hp==0, not yet flagged dead, combat_aux[10]==3) into a caller-provided buffer; return how many entries were collected.
logic_summary: drop_count=0; for i in 0..party_member_count: let pChar = runtime_char_array + i*0x50; if (pChar.flags & CHARFLAG_DEAD)==0 (not yet marked dead) && pChar.combat_aux_block[10]==3 (drop entry ready, type==scripted) && pChar.hp_current==0 (lethally hit): memmove(out_buffer + drop_count*3, &pChar.combat_aux_block[10], 3); drop_count++. return drop_count. Tail-calls into the shared POP/RET epilogue of fd2_count_active_chars_for_team_filter (JMP 0x1B64D) to return the count in EAX.

params.name: out_buffer
params.semantics: Pointer to the destination buffer that receives the packed 3-byte drop entries (one per dying char). Caller fd2_execute_ai_offensive_spell passes a 12-byte local drops_buffer. Entries are written contiguously at out_buffer + drop_count*3.
params.reason: Descriptive of role (output destination buffer); no address residue; matches body usage as the memmove destination base.

returns.semantics: Number of 3-byte drop entries collected (0..party_member_count). Consumed by fd2_process_battle_drop_entries as its entry count after the death animation completes.

notes: Source (btl_turn.c:350-369) verified semantically equivalent to Ghidra decomp via struct layout in types.h: pChar[5]=flags(+0x05,bit0=dead); pChar[0x31]=combat_aux_block[10] (combat_aux_block@+0x27, +10=0x31); *(uint16*)(pChar+0x40)=hp_current(+0x40); RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE=0x50, CHARFLAG_DEAD=0x01 (consts.h). Single caller: fd2_execute_ai_offensive_spell @0x15311 (UNCONDITIONAL_CALL @0x15433), step 11, called between spell-hit and death-flicker animation; collected entries later applied by fd2_process_battle_drop_entries @0x1AA1D (each 3-byte entry = byte type {0=item,1=gold,2=event,3=dialog} + ushort value). Source comment already concise and accurate (all 3 gate conditions + return); Ghidra plate detailed and consistent with refined understanding -> no edits to src or plate.
